sdkVersionAtPass._measured: resolved via readlink -f on node_modules/@civitai/*, cross-checked against each resolved package's own version field. NOT a pnpm store version count -- the store retains pre-upgrade entries, so it reports both versions after a clean bump and one each before it.

decisions.chose: leave every surface on the host's --civitai-* tokens
decisions.because: src/theme.ts contains ZERO hardcoded colour literals (measured: 0 hex matches), so light/dark correctness is already entirely the platform's. Moving to `skin` would transfer that debt to this app for no gain the store assets do not already provide -- the #DB6EC9 orchid plate is the brand's expression in the STORE (brand/icon.svg, brand/cover.svg, both attached and approved on the listing), not inside a block whose job is to render other people's images side by side.

decisions.what: no in-app hero image, despite hero generation being pre-authorised
decisions.because: the app's primary object is a configuration form that becomes a comparison grid, inside an iframe with minHeight 600. A hero band would push the prompt field -- the first thing anyone needs to touch -- further down on every visit. Same reasoning that kept sensei and model-benchmarking heroless. The store listing already carries generated cover art.

decisions.what: the concept band's hardcoded numbers now say `Example:` in the VISIBLE text
decisions.chose: mark them where a sighted reader can see it, and delete the aria-label that used to carry the marker
decisions.because: measured live on 0.8.6 at the default selection, the configure screen showed THREE different cell counts at once: this band's fixed `2 models x 2 styles = 4 cells`, the live counter's `2 of 12 cells`, and the button's `Generate Matrix - 2 cells`. The band reuses the same `2` a small selection has, so it read as a fourth opinion about the current state. The marker DID exist -- in `aria-label="Example: ..."` on a role-less <div>, which is not reliably announced by AT at all AND made the accessible name disagree with the visible text. That is also why the a11y sweep reads 0 violations here: every axe check passes on a non-interactive div that has a name. Removing the label and putting the word on screen makes the a11y tree and the screen say the same thing.

decisions.chose: rename to what it does rather than make it first-run
decisions.because: its call site is `{inBuild && ...}` and the build phase is re-entered via `New run`, so it rendered on EVERY visit to the configure screen, not once -- the name was a false claim. It cannot be MADE first-run either: remembering a dismissal needs `useAppStorage`, and that surface is gated by `assertViewerIsAppDeveloper` (mods + app-dev-testers), so for an ordinary viewer the flag could never be read back. model-benchmarking's `one-time dismissible panel with a persisted per-viewer flag` is therefore not portable to this app.

decisions.what: the per-cell Buzz copy in the header was left in place, though it is arguably redundant with the live counter
decisions.chose: do not delete standing money disclosure to save a line
decisions.because: phase 2 says to delete copy that explains what the UI already shows, and `Each cell spends only its real cost...` does overlap the counter's `max -- real cost is usually far less`. But the header copy is the only STANDING statement of the 200-Buzz per-gen cap; the counter's equivalent lives in a Tooltip. Demoting a money disclosure from standing copy to a hover is a downgrade in honesty, which is the opposite of what this arc is for. Decluttering is not worth it here.

decisions.what: phases 4 (identity) and 5 (moderation) are n-a, and this was MEASURED rather than assumed
decisions.chose: record the reason, do not invent a surface to grade
decisions.because: gen-matrix declares exactly one scope, `ai:write:budgeted`, and uses NO shared storage -- `useSharedStorage` appears nowhere in src/. There is no cross-user content, so there is nobody to attribute and nothing to report. A shared-storage board was considered and deliberately deferred (see deferred[]).

deferred.what: a shared-storage board of published comparison grids, so the expensive answer this app produces becomes readable by people who did not pay for it
deferred.blockedBy: the platform's publish path is author-cohort-only. `blocks.publishGenerationOutputs` calls `assertViewerIsAppDeveloper`, which is `mod OR the app-dev-testers cohort` and fail-closed, so an ordinary viewer cannot publish images at all. The READ side is deliberately open (`blocks.getImagesByIds` is commented `NOT the author gate: a viewer of the app can read images the app published`), so only half the loop exists. Per-user KV (`useAppStorage`) carries the same author gate; shared storage itself is genuinely public.
deferred.closingCondition: The author gate comes off the publish path: `assertViewerIsAppDeveloper` no longer guards `publishGenerationOutputs` in civitai/civitai `src/server/routers/blocks.router.ts`. That is a one-command mechanical check at the ref (`git -C <civitai> show origin/main:src/server/routers/blocks.router.ts | grep -A30 'publishGenerationOutputs: publicProcedure'`), and whoever runs the next phase 0 on this app is who checks it. Until then a board would be an operator-curated reading room, not a community board -- which the operator considered and declined on 2026-09-04.

deferred.what: an inline boot-theme reader in index.html, so the pre-`ready` paint uses the HOST's theme instead of the machine's OS preference
deferred.blockedBy: nothing, as of the SDK bump to app-sdk 0.37.0 -- this is now a CHOICE, not a blocker. `blocks/initFragment`'s `parseBlockInitFragment(hash)` returns `{ theme?, renderMode?, blockInstanceId? }` read synchronously at document parse time. src/bootTheme.ts's `bootThemeGuess()` already reads `data-civitai-boot-theme` FIRST and is deliberately forward-compatible, so only the inline reader is missing. It was not taken here because it changes the boot path and does not belong in a taste pass whose other changes are cosmetic and copy-level.
deferred.closingCondition: index.html gains the inline reader AND the tripwire in src/bootTokens.test.ts (`expect(BOOT_CSS).not.toContain('data-civitai-boot-theme')`) is replaced with assertions over the new override blocks, in the SAME commit -- a boot path whose CSS and reader disagree is a colour flash. The test failing is the mechanical signal; whoever writes the reader is who checks it.
